scope: Repeats the bounded raw /dev/nvme0n1 direct-read pathway after installing a desktop-size NVMe heatsink, using the same 64 GiB range, 1 GiB checkpoints, per-chunk SHA-256, detached service, and persistent watcher as the failing run.

mitigation.change: A desktop-size heatsink was installed on the CT4000T700SSD3 before this test.

test.mode: read-only direct I/O, per-GiB checkpoint and SHA-256

result.effective_rate: 594 MiB/s over the complete 64 GiB run

before.result: host access wedge after the run stopped answering

comparison.interpretation: The installed heatsink removed the immediate thermal/controller pathway under the previously failing raw-read protocol. The 45.00 C peak reduction and simultaneous throughput improvement make insufficient NVMe cooling the dominant physical cause of the earlier wedge.

checks.name: raw-read
checks.result: 64 of 64 checkpoints passed; status.tsv ended in passed

checks.name: progress-summary
checks.result: 64 rows, 0 nonzero exits, 0 missing hashes, all elapsed times 1 second

checks.name: watcher-window-summary
checks.result: peak 40.85 C, peak I/O PSI full avg10 0.69, maximum D-state 0, maximum inflight 0

checks.name: post-smart-and-journal
checks.result: SMART stayed clean and the warning-priority journal window was empty

non_claims: The physical heatsink mass, contact pressure, airflow, and SSD power draw were not measured.
Watcher temperature coverage is sampled, not a continuous thermal record; unobserved sub-sample peaks remain possible.
This test covers only the first 64 GiB logical range, not the complete 4 TB drive or every thermal environment.
Passing this raw block read does not by itself requalify the source GGUF; that requires the separate exact-file two-pass result.
The exact firmware, controller, or EC protection action that ended the prior boot remains unobserved.
